inputs.root_cause: SAL-UBL-OBL-0996E6D7B91D544F documented that model/typed.py's find()/find_all() match children by local name only, confirmed to be exploitable via a spoofed same-local-name element in an attacker-controlled namespace. The obligation's own finding explicitly declined a full fix as out of scope, citing ~78 call sites across the typed-projection layer as too large a blast radius for a citation-audit tick.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 7 new tests prove: find() itself remains naively vulnerable (documented, not hidden), but validate() now detects and rejects any document containing same-local-name siblings in different namespaces -- at the root level, nested deeper in the tree, regardless of spoofed-vs-real ordering, with the diagnostic naming both namespaces -- while a control test confirms no false positive on a namespace-clean document, and a dedicated test confirms the check correctly does not recurse into opaque ext:ExtensionContent (which legitimately holds arbitrary vendor content this package never queries by field name).
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Re-read the obligation's own finding in full, including its explicit reasoning for deferring a full fix: 'Fixing this properly requires auditing and updating every call site... a cross-cutting change with real blast radius, out of scope for a citation-audit tick to safely execute without dedicated design and regression coverage.' Confirmed via grep that ~78 call sites of find()/find_all() exist across the typed-projection layer, validating that this original assessment was correct.

2. Considered and rejected a narrower per-field namespace-allowlist approach (checking each call's expected namespace) as still requiring per-call-site knowledge equivalent to the full rewrite. Instead designed a detection-only defense: validate() flags the one structural signature every spoofing attempt of this shape must produce -- two or more same-local-name children in different namespaces under one parent -- without touching find()/find_all() or any of their 78 call sites at all, reducing blast radius to zero on the existing query primitives.

3. Verified the exact reproduction case from the original finding interactively: constructed a document with a spoofed {urn:evil:attacker:namespace}ID sibling ahead of the real {urn:oasis:...CommonBasicComponents-2}ID child -- confirmed find() still (dangerously, as documented) returns the spoofed value, but the new validate() check correctly flags the document as invalid with a ubl.namespace.shadowed_element diagnostic naming both namespaces.

4. Ran the full pre-existing ubl suite (878 tests, zero changes yet to any fixture) against the new check before writing any new test, specifically to look for false positives -- all 878 passed unchanged, strong empirical confirmation that no legitimate UBL document in this package's entire existing corpus produces the same-local-name-different-namespace shape the check flags.

5. Deliberately excluded ext:ExtensionContent subtrees from the walk: that wrapper legitimately holds arbitrary, opaque vendor content this package never queries via find()/find_all() by field name, so applying the check inside it would be a false-positive risk rather than a real protection -- verified directly with a dedicated test using two different-namespace vendor elements inside one ExtensionContent, confirming no diagnostic fires.

6. Wrote 7 formal tests: the documented find()-vulnerability caveat itself, the spoofing-detected case, order-independence (spoofed-first and real-first both caught), diagnostic message content, a no-false-positive control, nested-tree detection, and the ExtensionContent exclusion. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (885 passed, was 878, +7), and the full 6-format regression (3251 passed, was 3244, +7; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

7. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-9e80ff4727501f49, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ubl/ -q -- 885 passed, was 878 passed (878 passed unchanged BEFORE writing new tests, confirming zero false positives against the existing corpus)

.venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3251 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3244 passed
